instructions.name: close_market_v0
docs: Close an empty market and return its rent to `rent_recipient`.

accounts.name: rent_recipient
docs: Receives the market's rent.

accounts.name: authority
docs: Registered as the market's config authority. It need not sign, because
the market's own signature below already binds initialization to the
account's creator. A program PDA can therefore hold the role from the
start.

accounts.name: place_authority
docs: Registered as the market's place authority. It is an account rather
than an argument, because a duplicated account costs one index byte in
the transaction.

accounts.name: market
docs: Pre-created zeroed account, sized by [`ClobMarketV0::space_for`] for the
wanted capacity. That is about 98KB, which is above the CPI allocation
limit, so the client creates the account.
[`crate::instructions::resize_market_v0`] grows it later.
It signs, which binds initialization to the account's creator. The
client creates the account with a keypair, and the System program
already requires that keypair to sign the allocation, so the signature
costs an honest caller nothing. Without it, creation and initialization
may land in different transactions. Anyone may then initialize the
account first and name themselves `authority`. The operator's own call
then fails and the rent is stranded.

instructions.name: next_cross_v0
docs: Read-only. Reports the best matchable order on each side. Any cross
settles between those two orders. A caller simulates it, like
`next_removal_v0`.

instructions.name: next_removal_v0
docs: Read-only. Names the order the book lets a caller remove next. A caller
simulates it to find work, then sends the removal it names.

instructions.name: order_rules_v0
docs: Read-only. Reports what the book requires of an order before it holds
one. A caller builds against these rules instead of learning them from
a rejection.

instructions.name: orders_v0
docs: Read-only. Reports what the book holds for a set of refs, one answer
per ref. A ref that no longer names a live order comes back as
`OrderViewV0::NONE`.

instructions.name: propose_market_authority_v0
docs: Name the key that may take over this market's config. It takes over
only when it signs `accept_market_authority_v0`.

instructions.name: set_crank_conditions_v0
docs: Register the resolvers for this book's own crank conditions. The book
states when a turner must wake. The program that owns the flow states
what to do. Returns the account offset the condition block sits at, for
the watch registration.

errors.name: InvalidOrderParams
errors.msg: Order price/size is zero or user is default

errors.name: PriceNotTickAligned

errors.name: SizeNotStepAligned

errors.name: OrderTooSmall
errors.msg: Order size is below min_order_size

errors.name: SideAtCapacity

errors.name: StaleOrderRef
errors.msg: Order ref is stale: node is free or holds a different order

errors.name: OrderUserMismatch
errors.msg: Order ref does not belong to the given user

errors.name: MathError
errors.msg: Math overflow

errors.name: InvalidActivationDelay
errors.msg: Activation delay above max_activation_delay_slots

errors.name: MaxTsInPast
errors.msg: max_ts is in the past

errors.name: InvalidAuthority
errors.msg: Signer does not match the market authority for this operation

errors.name: ResponseTooLarge
errors.msg: Response exceeds the response buffer

errors.name: InvalidCapacity
errors.msg: Resize must grow the arena

errors.name: InvalidConfig
errors.msg: Market config out of bounds

errors.name: StaleUserSet
errors.msg: Deprecated: an unreachable maker ends the walk and is reported, it no longer fails

errors.name: BelowEvictThreshold
errors.msg: Side is below evict_threshold_per_side; nothing to evict

errors.name: OrderNotExpired
errors.msg: Order is not expired

errors.name: NodeIndexOutOfRange
errors.msg: Node index is outside the order arena

errors.name: ArenaExhausted
errors.msg: Order arena has no free node

errors.name: BookInvariantViolated
errors.msg: Book invariant check failed after the operation

errors.name: InvalidResponseLevel
errors.msg: Response level has a zero price or size, or is not strictly best-first

errors.name: EventTooLarge

errors.name: TakerOriginCrossPending
errors.msg: Deprecated: a crossed taker-origin order is skipped, not rejected

errors.name: OversizedUserSet

errors.name: OrderWouldCross

errors.name: TakerOriginBound

errors.name: OrderNotTakerOrigin

errors.name: FillExceedsOrder

errors.name: MaxTsBeforeActivation

errors.name: MarketNotEmpty

errors.name: OrderNotLive

errors.name: MissingReferencePrice
errors.msg: A quote budget needs a reference price

types.name: CancelAllArgsV0
docs: `cancel_all_v0` arguments.

fields.name: user
docs: Whose orders to withdraw, verified against each node.

fields.name: force
docs: Sweep taker-origin remainders that have not reached their activation
slot as well. Liquidation sets this flag. Every other caller leaves it
clear, and the sweep then skips such an order and reports the call as
not exhaustive.

types.name: CancelAllOutcomeV0
docs: Return data of `cancel_all_v0`. Per-side totals rather than a list of
removals, because that is the shape open-order aggregates consume. The
caller does one unwind per side and one count, however many orders the
sweep took.

fields.name: bid_reduce_only_orders
docs: How many of the swept orders on each side were reduce-only. The caller
tracks reduce-only resting orders per user. It disarms exactly this
many when the sweep removes them, without a per-order report.

fields.name: exhaustive
docs: The sweep took every order it was asked for. False means the book stopped at its
per-call cap, which repeating the call clears, or passed over a taker-origin
remainder whose claim the book still honours, which clears itself.

types.name: CancelOrderArgsV0
docs: `cancel_order_v0` arguments.

fields.name: user
docs: Owner of the order, verified against the node.

fields.name: force
docs: Remove the order even when it is a taker-origin remainder that has not
reached its activation slot. Liquidation sets this flag. Every other
caller leaves it clear, which holds a taker to the auction window its
own order asked for.

types.name: CancelSidesV0
docs: Which sides a `cancel_all_v0` withdraws. The wire cannot express "neither",
which would leave a maker believing its quotes are gone. A book reads a side
as a book side and a caller as a position direction. Only the tags must agree.

fields.name: authority
docs: Admin able to configure the market.

fields.name: place_authority
docs: The only signer allowed to place, cancel or execute. It is velocity's
quoter CPI signer PDA. Velocity verifies the `User` authority and the
flow-attestation policy, including zero-delay activation, before it
CPIs here.

fields.name: order_tick_size
docs: Prices must be a multiple of this, in PRICE_PRECISION. The check runs
at placement and the stored price does not encode it. It can therefore
change without repricing the resting book.

fields.name: order_step_size
docs: Sizes must be a multiple of this (base precision).

fields.name: min_order_size
docs: Floor on order size so every resting order has real capital at risk.

fields.name: blocking_min_size
docs: Floor on the size of an order that may end a walk. Zero disables it.
A caller carries at most 48 users, so 49 orders at the top of book can
block the depth behind them. The walk steps over a smaller order.

fields.name: base_precision
docs: Base units per whole unit. Velocity perps use 1e9 and spot varies.
Immutable after init, because resting order sizes are denominated in
it.

fields.name: next_order_id
docs: Starts at 1 so a zeroed (freed) node can never match a live order id.

fields.name: worst_bid
docs: List tails, so eviction of the worst order is O(1).

fields.name: default_activation_delay_slots
docs: Default taker speed bump. These slots are added to the placement slot
to get `activation_slot` when the caller does not choose a delay.

fields.name: max_activation_delay_slots
docs: Upper bound on a caller-chosen activation delay (auction flow).

fields.name: unknown_user_grace_slots
docs: How far the caller's account set is allowed to lag the book.
The walk skips an order whose owner is absent while its age, measured
from `activation_slot`, is at most this. Past that the order ends the walk.

fields.name: evict_threshold_per_side
docs: Soft cap. `evict_worst` is allowed once a side holds at least this
many orders. Eviction runs through a velocity crank, which keeps the
evicted maker's margin aggregates exact. The buffer up to the per-side
hard cap is what the crank has to work with.

fields.name: market_index
docs: Velocity perp market index this book serves.

fields.name: max_quote_levels
docs: Per-market response/batch tuning, each bounded by its `*_CEILING`.

fields.name: next_expiry_ts
docs: The earliest `max_ts` any live order carries, or [`i64::MAX`] when no
live order expires. A removal recomputes it only when it took the order
that held the minimum, so the field may be earlier than the truth. It is
never later, because that would leave work nobody is woken for.

fields.name: next_activation_slot
docs: The earliest `activation_slot` any live order carries that has not yet
arrived, or [`u64::MAX`] when none is pending. A passing slot makes the
field stale without any write, so every mutation recomputes it when the
stored slot is no longer in the future.

fields.name: crank
docs: The relay conditions that wake a turner for this book's own work.
The book maintains them as it places and removes orders, so no caller
passes a second account. `set_crank_conditions_v0` names the resolvers.

fields.name: pending_authority
docs: The authority `propose_market_authority_v0` named, which
`accept_market_authority_v0` installs once it signs. Zero when no
rotation is open.

fields.name: padding
docs: Reserved bytes. A later field, such as a fee destination or a
paused-operations bitmap, can claim them without moving `response`,
changing the account size, or migrating every live market. The bytes
must stay zero until a field claims them.

fields.name: taker_origin_head
docs: Oldest taker-origin order on each side, indexed by [`SideV0`] (bid 0, ask
1). [`NIL`] when the side holds none. The list is in rest order. A
taker-origin order is a migrated taker remainder that claims depth on
the other side, so a read of a side enumerates it. See [`crate::book`].

fields.name: taker_origin_tail
docs: Newest taker-origin order on each side, so an append is O(1).

fields.name: taker_origin_count
docs: Taker-origin orders on each side. Bounds the claimant hops one read of
a side may take, so a corrupt list cannot spin.

fields.name: reservation_grace_slots
docs: Slots past its activation slot for which a taker remainder's claim on
the depth it crosses is still honoured. Past the window the depth is
ordinary again, so a crank that never lands cannot hold the top of book
for ever. Zero ends the claim at activation.

fields.name: padding1
docs: Keeps `response` on the 8-byte step its records are cast at.

fields.name: response
docs: Scratch region that `quote_v0` and `execute_v0` stream their response
into. Return data carries a [`ResponsePointerV0`] that locates it. It is
the last field, so [`RESPONSE_OFFSET`] is the header size minus its
length. Its size holds the region's 8-byte start, so records cast in place.

types.name: ClobOrderRefV0
docs: Order handle. The node index is an O(1) hint the book verifies against the
order id, so a stale hint fails closed. `Clob` marks the one type here that
lands in velocity's IDL, beside `Order` and `OrderParams`.

types.name: ClobRemovalKindV0
docs: Which of the book's own removal cranks a caller is asking about. Both belong to the
book rather than the quoter interface, and a source with no resting orders has
neither. The caller asks rather than the book acting alone, because the caller owns
the consequence: a maker's margin, a reward, and a trigger slot.

types.name: ClobUpdateMarketArgsV0
docs: `update_market_v0` arguments. `None` leaves a setting unchanged. The book
checks the whole config after it applies every field, so one call can move
the step and the minimum together. The `Clob` prefix is there because this
type lands in velocity's IDL, as [`ClobOrderRefV0`] does.

types.name: CrankAccountV0
docs: One account a registered resolver takes, in the order its instruction
expects them. Restates `relay_spec::AccountRefV0` for the same reason
[`CrankResolverV0`] restates `CrankSpecV0`, and keeps `[u8; 32]` for the
same IDL-build reason.

types.name: CrankBlockV0
docs: Return data of `set_crank_conditions_v0`: the two regions of the market account a
registrant has to point relay at. A watch names an account, an offset and a length,
so reporting them lets a registrant watch without knowing this account's layout.

fields.name: block_offset
docs: Where the condition block starts.

fields.name: top_of_book_offset
docs: The region that changes whenever either side's best moves. A crossing order is
always a new best, so a watch here catches every cross. A caller that crosses
another source against this book needs a second watch, because repricing that
source writes nothing here.

types.name: CrankConditionsArgsV0
docs: `set_crank_conditions_v0` arguments: who resolves each of the book's own
conditions, and the accounts they all take. The book owns the wakes but
none of the answers, so the program that owns the flow registers what
runs. A zero `program` deactivates a condition.

types.name: CrankConditionsRecordV0
docs: `set_crank_conditions_v0` registered the resolver program for each of the
book's four conditions. A zero program deactivated that condition.

fields.name: account_count
docs: Accounts the registered resolvers take.

types.name: CrankResolverV0
docs: One resolver registration: which program answers a condition, with which
instruction, and what it must pay the keeper that lands the answer.
allow-verbose: explains why this restates `relay_spec::CrankSpecV0` instead of
reusing it. Relay's own type carries the same three fields, and the CLOB already
depends on `relay-spec`. But `relay-spec` deliberately depends on nothing but
`bytemuck`, so its `CrankSpecV0` derives neither `wincode`'s schema pair nor
anchor's borsh pair. Adding either there would put a wincode or anchor version
bound on every consumer of `relay-spec`, including ones with no CLOB in their tree.
`program` stays `[u8; 32]` rather than `Address`: anchor's IDL build derives
`IdlBuild` for its own `Pubkey` re-export, not for a bare `solana_address::Address`,
and `bun run program:idl` fails on this struct the moment the field is one.

types.name: DirectionV0
docs: Taker direction, from the taker's perspective. Encoded as its discriminant,
`Long = 0`. A direction inverted across the boundary fills the wrong side.

types.name: EvictWorstArgsV0
docs: `evict_worst_v0` arguments.

types.name: ExecuteArgsV0
docs: Arguments to `execute_v0`: commit a fill. [`QuoteArgsV0`] without the price
bound, because `size` is depth the caller chose off the ladder. A quoter may
fill less than `size`, and what it filled is the sum of its balance changes.
Every field must carry the value its quote carried.

fields.name: users
docs: Same contract as [`QuoteArgsV0::users`], and it leads for the same
reason.

fields.name: reference_price
docs: The mark the quote was taken against. A different price makes a quoter
that spends budgets pass over a different set of orders than it quoted.
A fill always has a mark, so a quoter may refuse `None` here.

types.name: ExecuteRecordV0
docs: One per execute. The record names orders by id only, which keeps the hot
path cheap. A reader resolves user and price against the indexer's order
table, which it builds from place records. Quote amounts come from price
times base.

fields.name: cancelled_client_order_ids
docs: Orders culled because the post-fill remainder fell below
`min_order_size`, by the placing caller's ids. See
[`OrdersCancelRecordV0::client_order_ids`].

types.name: FillArgsV0
docs: `fill_v0` arguments. A taker remainder resting here can aggress against sources
this program cannot see, such as a quoter or the vAMM, so velocity does that
matching and reports back. A list rather than a single fill, so a transaction that
resolves several remainders pays for one call.

types.name: FillEntryV0
docs: One taker remainder filled in a `fill_v0` batch. `price` is the remainder's
own resting price, the only price this program stores for it.

types.name: FillOutcomeV0
docs: Return data of `fill_v0`.

types.name: FillRecordV0
docs: One per `fill_v0`. `execute_v0` fills a taker against makers already on
this book, so [`ExecuteRecordV0`] can name the maker by id and leave price
and owner to the reader's order table. `fill_v0` instead reports a resting
taker remainder that aggressed against a venue this program never saw, so
the record carries the remainder's own price and owner rather than sending
a reader to a fill it cannot resolve any other way.

fields.name: cancelled_client_order_ids
docs: See [`ExecuteRecordV0::cancelled_client_order_ids`].

types.name: FillRequestV0
docs: One order the caller filled elsewhere, and by how much.

fields.name: client_order_id
docs: The placing caller's own id for this order. Every reader downstream of
velocity files orders under the caller's ids. The field lets such a
reader join a fill to an order without a map between the two id spaces.

types.name: FilledOrderV0
docs: What one order in a [`FillArgsV0`] came to.

fields.name: client_order_id
docs: The placing caller's own id, so a caller joins this to its own order
without holding a map between the two id spaces.

fields.name: culled_base_asset_amount
docs: Size dropped because the remainder fell under `min_order_size`. The
book will not hold it, so the caller unwinds it from the owner's
reservation.

fields.name: removed
docs: The order left the book, either filled out or culled.

types.name: L3ArgsV0
docs: Arguments to `quote_l3_v0`: how much of a side to describe. No user set and
no caps, because the question is what rests on the book, not what this
caller may settle.

fields.name: size
docs: Stop once this much base is described. Zero describes the side up to
`max_rows`.

fields.name: max_rows
docs: Stop after this many rows, whatever `size` is left.

fields.name: include_taker_origin_reservations
docs: Same contract as [`QuoteArgsV0::include_taker_origin_reservations`].

types.name: MarketAuthorityAcceptedRecordV0
docs: `accept_market_authority_v0` installed the proposed authority.

types.name: MarketAuthorityProposedRecordV0
docs: `propose_market_authority_v0` named a successor. A zero `proposed_authority`
withdraws the open proposal.

types.name: MarketCloseRecordV0
docs: `close_market_v0` closed an empty market and paid its rent to
`rent_recipient`.

types.name: MarketConfigV0
docs: Per-market configuration, set at init. It is also the init wire args.
`base_precision` and `market_index` are immutable afterwards.
`update_market_v0` updates the rest.

fields.name: blocking_min_size
docs: See [`ClobHeaderV0::blocking_min_size`]. Zero disables the floor.

types.name: MarketInitializeRecordV0
docs: `initialize_market_v0` created a market.

types.name: MarketResizeRecordV0
docs: `resize_market_v0` grew a market's arena.

types.name: MarketSettingsV0
docs: Every mutable setting of a market, as `update_market_v0` can change it.

types.name: MarketUpdateRecordV0
docs: `update_market_v0` changed a market's settings.

types.name: NextCrossV0
docs: Return data of `next_cross_v0`: the best matchable order on each side. Matchable is
the book's own predicate, meaning open, activated and unexpired, so a caller never
re-derives it. Any cross settles between these two heads. A caller compares their
prices and reads [`OrderViewV0::taker_origin`] to see which side came to trade.

types.name: NextRemovalArgsV0
docs: `next_removal_v0` arguments.

types.name: OrderEvictRecordV0
docs: Crank eviction at the soft cap. It is a separate record from a cancel,
because the UI shows an order as evicted or re-armed, and velocity re-arms
triggers in the same transaction.

types.name: OrderExpireRecordV0
docs: Crank reclamation of an expired order. An execute only skips an expired
order.

fields.name: client_order_id
docs: The placing caller's own id for this order. Every later record names
the order by this, so a reader files it under the id its own records
use and never holds a map between the two id spaces.

fields.name: flags
docs: [`crate::state::OrderBitFlag::TakerOrigin`] and
[`crate::state::OrderBitFlag::ReduceOnly`], at the same bit values.

types.name: OrderRulesV0
docs: Return data of `order_rules_v0`: what the book requires of an order before
it will hold one.
A caller that builds orders has to satisfy these, and finding out by
rejection costs it the transaction. Asking replaces reading them out of
the market account's header.

fields.name: min_order_size
docs: Floor on a resting order's size. A remainder below it cannot rest, and
the book culls one on its own fills. A caller re-placing a partially
filled remainder drops it instead of offering a placement the book
rejects.

fields.name: blocking_min_size
docs: Floor on the size of an order that may end a fill walk when its owner is not in
the caller's user set. The book skips a smaller order at any age. A maker sizing
a quote needs this, because it is what keeping price priority costs against a
caller that leaves the maker out. Zero disables the floor.

fields.name: default_activation_delay_slots
docs: Slots added to the placement slot to get `activation_slot` when the
caller chooses no delay. A caller that compares its own delay against
the book's own reads this value.

fields.name: max_activation_delay_slots
docs: Upper bound on a caller-chosen activation delay.

fields.name: place_authority
docs: The key the book requires to sign a placement, cancel, evict, expire or execute,
and the book's whole trust root. A caller pins it to its own signing PDA, so the
book only ever acts under a key the caller controls. `[u8; 32]` rather than
`Address`, for the IDL-build reason on [`CrankResolverV0::program`].

fields.name: tick_size
docs: The book's price and size grid. A caller that migrates an order pins these to
its market's grid at attach, so an aligned remainder always rests. An off-tick
rejection would revert the whole fill that carried it.

fields.name: side_order_counts
docs: Resting orders on each side right now, bids first. A side is full at
`arena_capacity / 2` and the book refuses a placement onto a full side, so a
caller predicts the refusal and fills without resting. The counts are a fact
about the slot this call ran in, not a rule.

fields.name: arena_capacity
docs: Order slots the whole arena holds. Half of it is the per-side cap.

fields.name: evict_threshold_per_side
docs: Count at which the eviction crank may take a side's tail. A side
between this and its cap still accepts placements, and the crank works
it back down.

fields.name: authority
docs: The key that may change these rules. A caller that mirrors them pins
it to its own signing PDA, so no rule changes without the caller.

types.name: OrderViewV0
docs: One order, as the book describes it to a caller. `next_removal_v0`,
`next_cross_v0` and `orders_v0` all answer with this shape, so the three
cannot drift apart. `order_ref.order_id == 0` means there is no such
order: ids start at one, and return data is a fixed width.

fields.name: client_order_id
docs: The caller's own id for this order, as supplied at placement.

fields.name: placed_slot
docs: Slot the order was placed in. A caller that prices a match against an
auction window needs it.

fields.name: max_ts
docs: The expiry the order carries, zero for good until cancelled.

fields.name: taker_origin
docs: The order is an unfilled taker remainder the caller migrated onto the
book. It demands liquidity rather than offering it, so a cross that
touches one settles at the other side's price.

types.name: OrdersArgsV0
docs: `orders_v0` arguments: which orders to describe. A caller holds refs from its own
records or from a client that read the book off chain, and cannot tell which still
name a live order. Asking replaces reading the arena.

fields.name: refs
docs: At most [`ORDER_VIEW_CEILING`] refs.

types.name: OrdersCancelRecordV0
docs: One per `cancel_all_v0`. A maker withdraws a whole side, or both sides, in
one instruction, rather than one [`OrderCancelRecordV0`] per order.
The record names orders by id only, under the same contract
[`ExecuteRecordV0`] uses. An indexer resolves price and size against the
order table it built from place records. The sweep's log therefore stays
four bytes per order instead of restating what the reader already holds.
Ids come in book order, bids before asks.
`exhaustive` false means the call stopped at
[`crate::state::CANCEL_ALL_ORDERS_CEILING`] and this user still has resting
orders. A reader must not treat the side as empty.

fields.name: sides
docs: Which sides the sweep covered, as the wire enum's tag
(0 = bids, 1 = asks, 2 = both).

fields.name: client_order_ids
docs: The swept orders, named by the placing caller's ids rather than the
book's. A bulk list is read by whoever files orders under those ids,
and carrying both would double the log for an id nothing downstream
asks for.

types.name: OrdersV0
docs: Return data of `orders_v0`: one [`OrderViewV0`] per requested ref, in the order they
were asked for. A ref that no longer names a live order comes back as
[`OrderViewV0::NONE`] rather than being dropped, so a caller reads the answers by
position. A race with a fill or a crank produces this, and it is not an error.

types.name: PlaceOrderArgsV0
docs: `place_order_v0` arguments.

fields.name: activation_delay_slots
docs: `None` takes the market's default activation delay. A value must be at
or under the market's maximum. Zero is allowed. The caller owns
attestation policy, and the book only clamps.

fields.name: max_ts
docs: Zero means good until cancelled.

fields.name: user
docs: The user the order settles against, in derivable form. The book trusts
its `place_authority` for identity. The caller verified control before
the CPI.

fields.name: taker_origin
docs: The order is an unfilled taker remainder the caller migrated onto the book,
which only the caller can know. The order cannot be taken while a live
counterparty crosses it, and a cross settles at the counterparty's price.

fields.name: client_order_id
docs: The caller's own id for this order. The book stores it and reports it
back on every answer that names the order, so the caller never holds a
map from the book's ids to its own. The book neither sorts nor
identifies orders by it. Zero means the caller keeps no id.

fields.name: reject_if_crossed
docs: Refuse the placement when the order would cross the opposite best price, rather
than resting it crossed. A crossed order still fills at its own price, so this
is about whether the order rests at all. A maker that quotes through the other
side has mispriced and would rather place nothing.

fields.name: reduce_only
docs: The order only reduces its owner's position. The book does not see
positions, so the caller declares this. At match time the book clamps a
fill against a reduce-only order to the owner's `base_cover` cap from
the execute call's user set.

fields.name: proposed_authority
docs: The zero address withdraws an open proposal.

types.name: QuoteArgsV0
docs: Arguments to `quote_v0`: what a taker wants, and who the caller can settle
against. `users` is a slice into the caller's instruction data, so a quoter
walks it without a copy in a 4 KB frame. It leads the struct to keep its
offset even, and a field added ahead of it must preserve that.

fields.name: users
docs: The loaded-user set, at most [`USER_SET_CAPACITY`] entries. A reader
checks that with [`user_set_within_capacity`], because the count comes
off the wire.

fields.name: size
docs: Base the taker wants filled.

fields.name: reference_price
docs: The price the caller marks a filled position at, in PRICE_PRECISION.
Budgets are spent and bands are checked against it. It does not bound
what a quoter may fill at. `None` is a read that settles nothing.

fields.name: taker
docs: The taker's own user, whose resting liquidity is skipped
unconditionally (self-trade prevention).

fields.name: limit_price
docs: The worst price the caller will fill at, in PRICE_PRECISION. Zero means
no bound. Not a trust boundary: a quoter that ignores it returns levels
the caller drops, and never widens what it may fill.

fields.name: taker_served_window
docs: Whether the taker's flow served a protection window before this call:
the swift hold, or the book's activation delay. The caller asserts it. A
quoter that serves only protected flow refuses when this is false.

fields.name: include_taker_origin_reservations
docs: Fill the depth that a taker-origin order reserves. Only the crank that
settles the cross sets it. A quoter that reserves no depth ignores it.

types.name: RemoveExpiredArgsV0
docs: `remove_expired_v0` arguments.

types.name: RemovedOrderV0
docs: Return data of `cancel_order_v0`, `evict_worst_v0` and
`remove_expired_v0`: the order that left the book.
`side` tells the caller whether the remaining size unwinds its bid-side or
ask-side reservation.

fields.name: client_order_id
docs: The caller's own id for this order, as supplied at placement.

fields.name: taker_origin
docs: The order was taker-origin. The flag tells a caller which side of the
cross it is resolving demanded liquidity, and therefore which side's
price the match settles at.

fields.name: reduce_only
docs: The order was reduce-only. A modify removes the order and rests an
equivalent one, and must carry the flag across. Otherwise the
replacement rests uncapped.

fields.name: max_ts
docs: The expiry the order carried, zero for good until cancelled. A modify removes an
order and rests an equivalent one, and this lets the caller carry the expiry
across without reading the book. Removal is the last moment it is knowable.

types.name: ResizeMarketArgsV0
docs: `resize_market_v0` arguments.

types.name: ResponsePointerV0
docs: Where in its response account a quoter wrote the response: the return data of
`quote_v0` and `execute_v0`. Declared once, so no two quoters can disagree
about which `u32` comes first.

types.name: SideV0
docs: Which side an order rests on: a bid makes its owner long, an ask short.

types.name: UserCapV0
docs: What one named user may still lose on the swept side, in quote. The quoter
has each fill price and the caller does not, so the cap is not in base. The
quoter charges `base * |price - reference_price| / BASE_PRECISION` where the
fill moves against the owner. Zero belongs in the exclusion bitmap.

fields.name: quote_cap
docs: `u64::MAX` is unbounded. It bounds depth that was margin-reserved at
placement. Base cannot express that bound, because a fill at a price in
the owner's favour costs nothing per base.

fields.name: base_cap
docs: The most base this user may give up on the swept side. `u64::MAX` is
unbounded. A book enforces it at match time and will not fill a reduce-only
order whose owner has no cap here, so for a book this field is a trust
boundary. Every other quoter reads it as advisory.

fields.name: index
docs: Index into the accompanying user set.

types.name: UserCapsV0
docs: Per-user room, parallel to the caller's user set. A user absent from all of
this is unconstrained. The quoter skips an excluded user's orders, and an
exclusion never fails the call. Not a trust boundary: the caller's own
post-fill checks still refuse the fill.

fields.name: excluded
docs: One bit per index in the set: set means no room on the swept side, so
pass that user's orders over.

fields.name: len
docs: Live entries at the head of `caps`. This crate fills the tail with the
entries of [`Self::EMPTY`], but a reader must not rely on the tail.

types.name: UserRefV0
docs: A velocity user in derivable form: the wallet and sub-account index that both
the `User` and `UserStats` PDAs derive from. An off-chain reader can reach every
user-derived account from a quoter's state alone. A stored `User` key cannot,
because its authority lives in account data the reader cannot load.
